subject: Urgent: Production 504s & retry storm impacting Parkway Health
messages:
From: Samantha Liu <samantha@parkwayhealth.com>
To: markus_klein <markus@redwood.ai>
Cc: Michael Baxter <mbaxter@parkwayhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Mar 2027 08:46:10 -0700
Subject: Production latency and 504s since 08:45 PDT

Markus —

We started seeing a major spike in 5xx/429s around 08:45 PDT this morning on Parkway's production traffic. Key observations from our side:
- Overall request success fell from ~99.6% to ~72%.
- 5xx rate ~18%, 429 rate ~12% (client dashboards).
- Queue depth reported by our client-side SDK jumped from ~20 concurrent inflight -> sustained ~1.2k, and many requests time out after routing to the API.
- Tail latency exploded: p50 ~120ms, p95 ~2.2s, p99 > 14s for generation endpoints.

We captured logs and a KV-cache snapshot and attached them (parkway-logs-20270322.tar.gz, kvcache-snapshot-08-45.json). We suspect retries from our front-end are worsening the situation but the cluster's queues look saturated even before most retries land.

This is impacting multiple critical flows (patient search and chart generation). Our infra on-call is standing by for an emergency call. Can you confirm receipt and an ETA for mitigation?

— Samantha
Samantha Liu
Head of Site Reliability, Parkway Health
From: markus_klein <markus@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Liu <samantha@parkwayhealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, evelyn_hart <evelyn@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 22 Mar 2027 08:52:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production latency and 504s since 08:45 PDT

Thanks for the heads up, Samantha — we see the same on our telemetry and are treating this as P0.

Immediate actions I am asking the team to take now:
1) Short-term mitigation (next 30–60m):
   - Ask Parkway to temporarily disable aggressive client-side retries (we'll provide a safe backoff)
   - Re-route a fraction of traffic to the conservative model variant (lower memory batch-friendly path) to relieve hotspots
2) Engineering triage: loop in runtime Eng to validate whether recent batching/KV-cache changes correlate with the spike. If so, prepare an urgent rollback of the batching kernel change.
3) Ops: scale up worker pool where possible and open a dedicated Slack war-room.

Evelyn — can you confirm whether we can roll back the batching kernel in a controlled manner and the expected impact window? Marissa / Lauren, please prepare the customer comms and an executive brief. I'll join the war room.

Markus
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
From: evelyn_hart <evelyn@redwood.ai>
To: markus_klein <markus@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 22 Mar 2027 09:10:35 -0700
Subject: Re: Production latency and 504s since 08:45 PDT

Quick triage notes (runtime eng):
Observations: the runtime traces show batching queues saturating and KV-cache eviction rates spiking at 08:44–08:46. The pattern is consistent with a cache-thrashing scenario: a recent change to the batch coalescer + a subtle KV-cache hash mismatch causes many requests to miss the cache and trigger heavy backend work, which back-pressures the batching queue and produces long tails. That explains both the p99 jump and the 429/504 amplification when clients retry.

Suggested immediate mitigations (I can run these if approved):
- Roll back the batching kernel change to tag v1.18.3 (this should reduce the batch coalescing aggressiveness that produces the hot stranding). Estimated deploy & warm-up: 12–18 minutes.
- Temporarily pin Parkway traffic to the conservative model variant (model-fallback-2027-02) that uses a serial execution path with lower concurrency pressure.
- Apply a short-lived rate limit on the public route for Parkway to cap client retries (we'll coordinate a nonce-based bypass for critical admin endpoints).

I've prepared a rollback patch and runbook (rollback_plan_v2.md) and can push the rollback as soon as I get green from Markus. Note: full cache warm-up will take ~20–30 minutes post-rollback.

— Evelyn
Senior Software Engineer, Runtime
From: Samantha Liu <samantha@parkwayhealth.com>
To: markus_klein <markus@redwood.ai>
Cc: Michael Baxter <mbaxter@parkwayhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Mar 2027 09:18:45 -0700
Subject: Re: Production latency and 504s since 08:45 PDT

Thanks — we can flip off client retries from our side for the next hour and accept traffic pinning to a conservative variant. Please prioritize the rollback if you believe that is the root cause. This is triggering our on-call paging; our CTO has been looped in.

Can you provide an ETA for the rollback and an expected customer-facing impact (success rate improvement + approximate time to recovery)? We also need a short status note to our execs ASAP.

— Samantha
From: markus_klein <markus@redwood.ai>
To: evelyn_hart <evelyn@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 22 Mar 2027 09:35:22 -0700
Subject: Re: Production latency and 504s since 08:45 PDT

Plan confirmed and executing now:
- Evelyn is pushing the rollback to tag v1.18.3 immediately (target complete ~09:48 PDT).
- Ops to increase worker pool by 30% for Parkway shard and pin Parkway to model-fallback-2027-02.
- CS (Marissa) to draft the one-paragraph status update for Parkway execs; include estimated time-to-recovery and offer credits if downtime persists beyond 4 hours.

Evelyn — please post status updates in the #war-room channel and attach the rollback PR when created. Lauren — please prep an internal exec brief (1 pager) for Jonas.

Markus
From: jonas_weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
To: markus_klein <markus@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, evelyn_hart <evelyn@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 23 Mar 2027 11:04:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Production latency and 504s since 08:45 PDT

Thanks for the quick triage. A few exec-level asks to close out the escalation: 
1) RCA timeline — I need a blameless RCA note on my desk within 48 hours covering: root cause, why the batching/KV-cache interaction wasn't caught in staging, and mitigation to prevent recurrence.
2) Customer comms — final copy for Parkway execs and a post-incident note to the account owner (include ETA and credits if applicable).
3) Immediate risk actions — confirm whether the rollback is permanent or temporary; if temporary, provide a clear rollout plan for a safe re-introduction of the batching change with canaries and test harnesses.
4) Finance/credits — coordinate with Sales/Finance to propose a goodwill package; cc Lauren on the ask.

Please escalate any blockers to me directly. We'll schedule a 09:00 war-room check-in tomorrow to review the RCA draft and customer messaging.

— Jonas
VP, Product Operations, Redwood Inference
